# Implementation Plan: Editing Users and Classes

The current UI contains interactive elements (Active Classes cards, User edit pen icon) that are visually clickable but lack event handlers. Additionally, the backend does not currently support `PUT` requests for Users and Classes.

This plan will introduce the necessary endpoints and hook them up to the UI.

## Proposed Changes

### Backend API
- **[MODIFY]** `backend/src/admin/admin.controller.ts`:
  - Add `@Put('users/:id')` endpoint mapped to `updateUser`.
  - Add `@Put('classes/:id')` endpoint mapped to `updateClass`.
- **[MODIFY]** `backend/src/admin/admin.service.ts`:
  - Implement `updateUser(id, data)` to update `name`, `role`, and `plan`.
  - Implement `updateClass(id, data)` to update `courseTitle`, `time`, and `level`.

### Frontend Store
- **[MODIFY]** `src/store/admin-store.ts`:
  - Add `updateUser: (id: string, userData: any) => Promise<void>` action.
  - Add `updateClass: (id: string, classData: any) => Promise<void>` action.

### Frontend Components
- **[MODIFY]** `src/app/admin/users/UsersClient.tsx`:
  - Add a `handleEditUser(user)` function using browser `prompt`s (similar to the existing `handleAddUser` function) to update the user's name and role.
  - Attach `onClick={() => handleEditUser(user)}` to the pen icon button.
- **[MODIFY]** `src/app/admin/classes/ClassesClient.tsx`:
  - Add a `handleEditClass(cls)` function using browser `prompt`s to update the class time/schedule.
  - Attach `onClick={() => handleEditClass(cls)}` to the Active Class cards.

## Open Questions
- Is using simple browser `prompt`s sufficient for this iteration of editing, or do you prefer full React Modal components? (I propose `prompt`s to match the existing `handleAddUser` implementation and keep it simple for now).

## Verification Plan
- Click a class card -> should prompt for new time -> should update in UI and database.
- Click a user edit icon -> should prompt for new details -> should update in UI and database.
We want to ensure everything work for all profiles for now we are fixing the ui on the admin side - see the implementation plan

"# Walkthrough: Implementing User and Class Editing

I've implemented the changes from the provided implementation plan to allow editing Users and Classes via the Admin Dashboard.

## Changes Made

### Backend API
- Added `PUT /api/admin/users/:id` endpoint in `backend/src/admin/admin.controller.ts` mapped to a new `updateUser` method in `backend/src/admin/admin.service.ts`.
- Added `PUT /api/admin/classes/:id` endpoint in `backend/src/admin/admin.controller.ts` mapped to a new `updateClass` method in `backend/src/admin/admin.service.ts`.

### Frontend Store
- Added `updateUser` and `updateClass` actions to the global Zustand store in `src/store/admin-store.ts` to seamlessly perform the `PUT` requests and refresh the respective lists.

### UI Components
- **User Editing:** Updated `src/app/admin/users/UsersClient.tsx` to include an `onClick` handler on the edit (pen) icon. Clicking it now prompts the admin to update the user's name and role, and saves the updates to the database.
- **Class Editing:** Updated `src/app/admin/classes/ClassesClient.tsx` to include an `onClick` handler on the active class cards. Clicking a class card now prompts the admin to update the class's scheduled time, and saves the updates to the database.

## Validation
- Clicking on a user's edit icon prompts for the new `name` and `role`. 
- Clicking on an active class card prompts for a new `time`.
- The frontend store automatically refetches and updates the displayed data after a successful edit.
